request.query: AI cloud company price hike for Nvidia GPU rental from October November

results.title: Nebius GPU Price Hike: H100 to B300 Cloud Prices Rise | metir Blog
results.author: Metir AI Team
highlights:
Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices up to 21% on October 1, 2026, its second hike in months. What H100 to B300 cloud prices say about AI compute costs.

Metir AI Team October 8, 2026 8 min read

On October 1, 2026, the Nebius GPU price hike took effect: the neocloud raised on-demand rates for Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 instances by roughly 17% to 21%. Nebius's own pricing page now lists the new rates with that effective date and notes that prices exclude taxes and may change at any time (Nebius pricing). It is the second increase in a few months, and it runs against the story most people remember from 2024 and 2025, when GPU rental prices mostly fell.

$3.85 to $4.50 H100 per GPU-hour (+17%)

$4.50 to $5.40 H200 per GPU-hour (+20%)

$7.15 to $8.50 B200 per GPU-hour (+19%)

$7.85 to $9.50 B300 per GPU-hour (+21%)

NVIDIA

AMD

The hike covers Nvidia GPU instances and AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity.

...

Nebius's pricing page lists these on-demand rates per GPU-hour, before and from October 1: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, H200 $4.50 to $5.40, B200 $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (Nebius pricing). Our arithmetic on those figures gives 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%, matching press coverage.

...

The increase is not limited to GPUs. Stocktwits, citing a notice to customers, reports that AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU pricing rose from $0.012 to $0.015 per vCPU-hour (25%) and Genoa memory from $0.0032 to $0.0045 per GiB-hour (about 41%) (Stocktwits). Silicon UK adds that customers who reserve large clusters for several months can still receive discounts, and that the cumulative B300 increase across the two hikes is 56% (Silicon UK).

The earlier move came in May 2026. Yahoo Finance reported that Nebius would lift on-demand H100 rates from $2.95 to $3.85 per hour, about 29%, and that preemptible capacity rose 51% (Yahoo Finance). Put together, an H100 hour that cost $2.95 in spring costs $4.50 today, a rise of about 53% by our arithmetic.

...

Early coverage disagreed about sourcing. Stocktwits said the details came from Nebius's communication to customers, reshared on Reddit and X, with no official public statement in its report. Silicon UK treated the rates as a Nebius announcement. The question is now largely settled by the company's own pricing page, which shows the October 1 rates. The two reports also differ slightly on timing: Stocktwits was published late on September 16, while Silicon UK dated its report September 18 and said Nebius announced the change "on Thursday."

...

- Demand outrunning supply. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress said on an earnings call that rental prices for older Hopper GPUs had risen about 20% year to date, and that rental demand still exceeded supply (Yahoo Finance). Silicon UK quotes Nebius calling the move "an indication of sustained demand for training and deploying AI models," and notes CoreWeave said the same day it was signing new contracts at higher prices (Silicon UK).
- Memory costs. The 41% memory increase fits the wider shortage in DRAM and HBM, which we covered in our memory supercycle analysis. Nebius has not, in the sources we reviewed, said how much of the increase is cost pass-through versus pricing power.

...

List prices are an input to a budget, not the budget itself, but the arithmetic is worth doing. Take 1,000 H100-hours:

| Scenario | Price per GPU-hour | Cost of 1,000 H100-hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spring 2026 (before May hike) | $2.95 | $2,950 |
| Summer 2026 (before October) | $3.85 | $3,850 |
| From October 1, 2026 | $4.50 | $4,500 |

The October step alone adds $650 per 1,000 hours. Counting both hikes, the same hours cost $1,550 more than in spring. For a Blackwell workload, 1,000 B300-hours moves from $7,850 to $9,500, an extra $1,650.

The impact differs by workload:

- Training runs that rent a large cluster for weeks or months can usually negotiate reserved or committed pricing below on-demand list rates, though that requires a commitment and a sales process.
- Bursty inference and experimentation typically sits on on-demand rates, so it takes the full increase and has the least room to plan around it.
- Spot or preemptible capacity is cheaper but, per the May report, has also been repriced upward.

results.title: Nebius October Price Increase: Recalculate Startup Runway | Lunera
highlights:
Nebius’s October 1, 2026 on-demand GPU price increases are now effective, with H100, H200, B200 and B300 rates up roughly 17%–21%. Recalculate startup runway using the additional cost of exposed usage—not the headline percentage. A 20% GPU price increase does not mean a 20% increase in company burn, and the price change alone is not a reason to migrate.

...

Source: Nebius public USD on-demand prices, as cited for October 6, 2026. Old → new: H100 $3.85 → $4.50; H200 $4.50 → $5.40; B200 $7.15 → $8.50; B300 $7.85 → $9.50 per GPU-hour.

## The Increase Applies To Specific Resources And Rates

As of October 6, 2026, Nebius’s public pricing page lists these USD on-demand rates per GPU-hour. Percentage increases are calculated from those prices.

| GPU | Old Rate | New Rate | Increase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | 16.9% |
| H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | 20.0% |
| B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | 18.9% |
| B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | 21.0% |

These are per GPU, not per multi-GPU VM, and exclude applicable taxes. The same page shows unchanged on-demand rates for RTX PRO 6000 and unchanged starting prices for L40S configurations.

The change also reaches some CPU-only workloads. Nebius’s compute documentation identifies increases for non-GPU AMD Epyc Genoa CPU and RAM, and non-GPU Intel Ice Lake RAM. Audit those resources separately; do not apply a blanket GPU percentage to the whole invoice. The figures above do not quantify the CPU and RAM increases.

For commitments or negotiated pricing, check your agreement and account-specific quote. A public list-price change does not establish what happens to an existing contract. The documentation also specifies separate ILS pricing for companies from Israel; the USD table is not a substitute for those rates.

...

Start with billed running time, not GPU utilization. Nebius bills running VM compute by the second; stopped VM compute is not charged, but storage remains chargeable. A running GPU waiting for work still belongs in your cost model.

results.title: Nebius moves spare GPU hours to spot prices | Wire
results.author: Sean
highlights:
# Nebius moves spare GPU hours to spot prices from $0.79

Nebius switched its spare GPU hours from a fixed price to live spot pricing on 8 October. An H100 hour now floats between $0.79 and $4.49. Nebius gets paid more when clusters are full. The stuck step is the idle hour, and only the console shows it.

...

Illustrative image. Nebius H100 preemptible price band from 8 Oct 2026.

`WIRE` · `NEOCLOUDS` · `GLOBAL` · Data as at 9 Oct 2026

Nebius no longer sells its spare GPU hours at a fixed price. Since 8 October 2026, its interruptible (preemptible) GPU hours float. An H100 hour now costs anywhere from $0.79 to $4.49. Until last week it was a flat $2.15. The price moves with how full Nebius's clusters are, and it can change every 15 minutes. On the neocloud model, this is the idle-hour step: Nebius now gets paid more for spare chips when they are scarce, and less when they sit.

## What happened

Nebius, the GPU cloud that rents Nvidia chips by the hour, updated its compute price list for October. Two changes, a week apart:

8 October

Preemptible B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 hours move to dynamic spot pricing

Nebius Compute pricing documentation

The band

Floor of $0.79 (H100, H200) or $0.99 (B200, B300). Ceiling one cent below the on-demand rate

Price set by capacity, cluster use, customer demand and pricing preferences

1 October

On-demand rates up 17% to 21%: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, B300 $7.85 to $9.50

This raised the spot ceiling too, since the ceiling tracks on-demand

Who can see the price

Current and past spot prices sit inside the Nebius console, not on a public page

...

A GPU earns money only in the hours someone rents it. An hour nobody buys is gone. Preemptible hours are how a cloud sells chips that would otherwise sit idle. The renter gets a cheap price, and Nebius can take the chip back when a full-price customer wants it.

...

Who gets paid. Nebius, when its clusters are full. A spare B300 hour that earned a flat $4.30 can now earn up to $9.49. The spot price also points spare chips at whoever values them most.

Who pays. Renters running batch jobs, tests and research on spare time. They used to know their price. Now they carry the price risk, on top of the risk of being kicked off.

Who waits. Buyers who want certainty. Nebius still sells multi-month cluster reservations at up to 35% off on-demand. The new spread makes that commitment look better to a renter.

...

The band is the published range, not what renters actually pay. Nebius has not said where spot prices have traded since 8 October.

Spare hours are a small slice of a GPU cloud's revenue. Most of the money comes from long contracts. This change tells you how Nebius prices its leftovers, not how much it earns.

...

Sources: Nebius, Compute pricing in Nebius AI Cloud, read 9 Oct 2026: from 1 Oct 2026 on-demand H100 $4.50 (was $3.85), H200 $5.40 (was $4.50), B200 $8.50 (was $7.15), B300 $9.50 (was $7.85); from 8 Oct 2026 preemptible pricing for B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 switches to dynamic spot pricing, preemptible from $0.79 (H100, H200, RTX PRO 6000) and from $0.99 (B200, B300), previously fixed at $2.15 (H100), $2.45 (H200), $3.95 (B200), $4.30 (B300) and $0.95 (RTX PRO 6000); spot prices can change as often as every 15 minutes and the highest is one cent below the on-demand rate; Nebius price page, read 9 Oct 2026: commitment discounts of up to 35% off on-demand for multi-month cluster reservations, current spot prices shown in the Nebius console; GPU Cloud Advisors, 28 Sep 2026: 1 Oct increase of 17% to 21%. The monthly server cost examples, the ceilings as a multiple of the old price, and the spread are our arithmetic. Not investment advice. Do your own research.

results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Going Up. The Token Price Is Not. - Tech Thought Leaders
results.author: Ivan Tarin
highlights:
Executive Summary

Rented GPU capacity is getting more expensive while the price of a token keeps falling. Nebius will raise on-demand rates for the H100, H200, B200 and B300 from 1 October, its second increase in three months, with the B300 up 21 percent to $9.50 a GPU hour. The memory tier moved further still, and Genoa memory rose about 41 percent.

The finding is that the floor under inference pricing is set by memory and power, not by the age of the silicon. Gartner still expects roughly a 90 percent fall in cost per token by 2030, and both things are true at once, because the tokens a GPU hour can produce climb faster than the rent does. Watch the spread between the two numbers. Either one read on its own will mislead you.

The cheapest way to buy AI compute is not getting cheaper. From 1 October, Nebius raises the on-demand rate for four Nvidia accelerators, and it is the second rise in three months. The number most teams track, cost per token, is still heading down.

Both of those live in the same market, which is why the gap between them is the story.

...

## The new rate card is not a rounding error

Nebius published the change on its own pricing page. The H100 moves from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, up 17 percent. The H200 rises 20 percent to $5.40. The B200 rises 19 percent to $8.50. The B300 takes the steepest step, up 21 percent to $9.50.

Add the three months since the previous change, and the B300 rate is up roughly 56 percent. The increases were not limited to accelerators. Nebius lifted the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU rate 25 percent and the Genoa memory rate about 41 percent.

Trackers saw the pressure earlier. SemiAnalysis recorded H100 one-year contract prices climbing from about $1.70 a GPU hour in October 2025 to $2.35 by March 2026, close to 40 percent.

...

Here is the mechanism. The newer the chip, the more high-bandwidth memory it carries, and memory has been the tightest part of the build, as memory

...

Per-token prices keep falling while the rented GPU hour climbs. Nebius raises four accelerator tiers on 1 October.

...

The falling number is real too.

...

The specialist clouds are pricing to that scarcity. CoreWeave has been lifting contracted power, from 3.1 gigawatts at the end of 2025 to 4.2 gigawatts by August, and JPMorgan moved its rating to Overweight on stronger compute pricing. Nebius reported second-quarter revenue of $582.3 million, with AI cloud revenue up 514 percent to $574.9 million.

results.title: GPU Pricing Forecast for AI Use - Sesame Disk
results.author: Rafael
highlights:
- Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates 17-21% on October 1, 2026: H100 to $4.50/hr, H200 to $5.40, B200 to $8.50, B300 to $9.50.
- CoreWeave (CRWV) has pushed through roughly 37.5% in cumulative price increases since July, and is signing short contracts near $40 million per megawatt.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block reservation prices about 20% on July 1, 2026, with P6-B300 at $14.04 per accelerator-hour.
- Runpod’s fleet data shows B200 list prices up 31% between January and August 2026, with high-bandwidth memory effectively sold out into 2027.
- Custom ASIC shipments are growing 44.6% in 2026 versus 16.1% for merchant GPUs, per TrendForce.

...

The clearest evidence comes from providers themselves. Nebius disclosed its October 1 card through customer communications reshared on Reddit and X. H100 hourly rates rose about 17% to $4.50, H200 rose 20% to $5.40, B200 nearly 19% to $8.50, and B300 about 21% to $9.50 from $7.85. CPU pricing moved too, with AMD (AMD) EPYC Genoa climbing 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour and Genoa memory up roughly 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour. NBIS shares jumped 9.15% premarket on September 17 when the hike surfaced, and the stock is up about 110% over six months, per GuruFocus.

...

The reversal is not limited to one neocloud. SemiAnalysis tracked Nvidia (NVDA) H100 one-year rental contracts climbing nearly 40% to $2.35 per GPU-hour in March 2026 from a $1.70 low in October 2025, as covered in this site’s August GPU price trends analysis. Runpod’s Fall 2026 State of AI Compute report, drawing on over 1.2 million users across 186 countries, found flagship GPU list prices rising through 2026, including a 31% B200 increase between January and August. The report’s framing is blunt: “Hardware is scarce, flagship GPU prices are rising, and AI bills are becoming material enough that teams can no longer treat the largest frontier model as the default answer to every problem,” according to the press release.

...

The neocloud hikes might be dismissed as a small-provider phenomenon, but AWS’s July 1 change confirms the trend at the top of the market. Amazon Web Services (AMZN) raised EC2 Capacity Block reservation prices for machine-learning GPU instances by about 20%, citing “supply and demand dynamics.” New per-accelerator hourly rates span the fleet: P6-B300 at $14.04, P6-B200 at $12.355, P5 in US regions at $5.191, P5e at $5.97, and P4de at $2.214, per Investing.com.

results.title: Nebius raises prices across the board on… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius raises prices across the board on October 1: H100 +17% to $4.50/hour, B300 to $9.50/hour

Trade press Slicast · October 6, 2026 at 21:09 UTC · Global · Source: Shattered.io

importance 78

N ebius, the Amsterdam-based neocloud provider, notified customers on September 17, 2026 that it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD CPU capacity, and memory starting October 1, 2026. It's the company's second price hike in three months, and this time the increases stretch well beyond GPUs into the CPU and memory tiers that most cloud budgets treat as an afterthought.

The numbers are specific. Nvidia H100 instances rise roughly 17% to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85, H200 climbs 20% to $5.40 from $4.50, B200 goes up about 19% to $8.50 from $7.15, and the newest B300 chips take the biggest hit at 21%, reaching $9.50 per GPU-hour from $7.85. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates jump 25%, and memory pricing rises about 41%, the steepest increase across the board. Investors read it as a sign of tight capacity, not weak demand: Nebius shares (Nasdaq: NBIS) jumped as much as 11.1% in pre-market trading the same day.

For a team running a sustained H100 workload, that 17% translates to an extra $0.65 per GPU-hour, which compounds fast across a multi-GPU training cluster running around the clock. What stands out is the memory line. A 41% jump on memory-backed capacity is the largest single increase Nebius applied, bigger than any of the GPU tiers. Memory rarely makes cloud pricing headlines because it's usually bundled into instance pricing rather than billed separately, but Nebius broke it out this time, which suggests memory availability, not just GPU silicon, is now a binding constraint on how much compute the company can actually deliver.

This is not an isolated move. Around May 2026, Nebius already raised on-demand capacity prices by an average of 29% and spot capacity by 51%. That means Nebius has now raised prices twice in under half a year, with the spring spot-market increase actually exceeding the September GPU hikes in percentage terms. Reuters framed the September move plainly: Nebius is raising prices because demand for computing power keeps rising faster than supply. It's closer to basic capacity rationing, the same mechanism that pushed cloud GPU rental rates up during the original 2023 H100 shortage, except this time it's spreading into CPU and memory tiers that used to be treated as commodity add-ons.

...

Cloud GPU pricing is notoriously hard to compare directly because providers mix spot, on-demand, reserved, and multi-year contract rates on the same public price list. But looking at H100 rental rates across the market as of September 2026 shows just how wide the spread is. RunPod offers H100 instances at $1.99–$2.99 per GPU-hour on demand and marketplace rates, Lambda at $3.29–$3.99 on-demand. Nebius now sits at $4.50 from October 1, CoreWeave at $4.25–$6.16 on-demand, and AWS's P5 instance pricing approaches $6.88 per GPU on a list-price basis. Nebius's increase moves it higher on the ladder but still below legacy hyperscalers, maintaining its position as a specialist provider with more capacity allocation and tighter pricing than the market leaders.

results.title: Amazon's GPU rental hike turns scarcity into a contract problem — The Spend Ledger
highlights:
Amazon raised EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing by 15% this week, and the cost lands wherever AI project commitments were made before the reset.

...

The Signal

Amazon raised prices on EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML by approximately 15% this week, with new rates taking effect the following week, according to MarketWatch and Yahoo Finance reporting on October 2, 2026. The increase covers reserved access to Nvidia accelerators across the A100-to-B300 range. That span matters because it is not one generation of chip; it is the entire stack that enterprise AI teams are actively queuing for. When the price resets mid-queue, the customer absorbs it before the previous reservation has finished paying back.

...

The mechanism here is specific and worth tracing. EC2 Capacity Blocks are not spot purchases. Buyers commit to a block of GPU time in advance, paying for guaranteed access rather than taking their chances in the on-demand market. That structure was designed to give enterprises predictability in a scarce-capacity environment. What it also does, by design, is give Amazon a clean price-reset point each time the market tightens. The vendor adjusts the block rate; the next buyer pays it; the prior commitment is already sunk.

...

The more valuable concessions are in contract terms: specific accelerator class and region committed by name, substitution rights if the vendor swaps chip generations, lead-time guarantees, and remedies if capacity slips after booking. A vendor willing to name the exact hardware and delivery date is offering something meaningfully different from one offering access to a capacity pool. Buyers who treat those as equivalent are pricing the wrong risk.

results.title: Compute Rents Rose 20% While Model Output Prices Halved · LEARN.INVEST
results.author: Steven
highlights:
The average price of a million large language model tokens fell from a June peak of $2.05 to about $0.95 at the end of September, more than halving in a little over three months and setting a low for the life of the index.

Over the same stretch, the machines that run those models got more expensive. The cloud compute provider Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates from October 1: the H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour and the B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, with increases across the range of 17% to 21%. It was the second rise since May, when the H100 was listed at $2.95.

The two prices move apart because different things set them. GPU rents reflect physical capacity that is currently short. Token prices reflect how model vendors choose to compete. OpenAI cut pricing on its GPT-5.6 Luna line by 80% in late July and the index followed it down. That was a pricing decision, not a drop in cost.

A lower unit price does not mean a smaller bill either. Token consumption rose more than a hundredfold over the same period, and many companies are paying more than they were six months ago. The squeeze lands in the middle: resellers and smaller providers who have no model of their own to discount, but who do pay the higher compute rate, are being pressed from both sides at once.

results.title: Amazon raises reserved AI chip rental prices by about 15% | Superpower Daily
results.author: Superpower Daily Editorial Desk
highlights:
The new rates are scheduled for the week after October 2. The service charges an upfront reservation fee plus an operating system fee.

...

Amazon is raising the price of reserved Nvidia AI-chip capacity by about 15 percent, with new rates scheduled for the week after October second, 2026. Quartz, citing MarketWatch, reports that the increase applies to Amazon’s EC2 Capacity Blocks for machine learning: a service that lets customers reserve access to Nvidia hardware, rather than buy the chips outright. The reservations span several generations, from A100 to B300, so the change is not limited to H100s. The bill has two pieces: an upfront reservation fee, plus a separate operating-system fee. So the hourly rate is not the whole cost, and the reservation fee isn’t simply charged one hour at a time. For scale, an eight-chip H100 instance, listed as p5.48xlarge, was priced at about $41.53 an hour in major U.S. regions before the change. Dividing evenly gives about $5.19 per chip-hour, though Amazon does not list that as a separate single-chip rental price. At the old rate, 24 hours comes to about $996.67, before the operating-system fee. Applying exactly 15 percent would put the instance near $47.76 an hour, but that’s a calculation—not Amazon’s confirmed new quote. The increase is approximate, and the actual updated rate for this eight-chip configuration remains unconfirmed until Amazon publishes revised pricing.

...

Customers reserving Nvidia chips through Amazon’s EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML face an approximately 15% price increase. Amazon announced the change with updated rates scheduled for the week following October 2, 2026, according to MarketWatch reporting cited by Quartz.

results.title: GPU rental without hyperscalers: How good are neo clouds?
results.author: Benedikt Langer
highlights:
At Lambda, an H100 GPU costs 3.55 euros an hour, against 10.95 euros at Azure, according to the price list of 4 October 2026. Neo clouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius and Lambda offer another option alongside hyperscalers. Several providers expand using secured loans. CoreWeave depends on a few large customers for much of its revenue.

...

- Neo clouds rent out primarily GPU compute time, and on the list prices for an H100 hour they sit well below AWS and Azure, though Nebius raised its H100 hourly rate by 17 percent on 1 October 2026.
- As of 30 June 2026, CoreWeave carried debt equivalent to 31.24 billion euros, and Microsoft accounted for roughly 67 percent of CoreWeave’s revenue in 2025.
- European capacity is being created at Telekom in Munich, at Nebius in Finland and France, and in up to seven planned EU gigafactories.

## One GPU, many price points

For an hour on an Nvidia H100 GPU, the range on 4 October 2026 is wide. The rates are only comparable to a limited extent. Lambda charges the equivalent of 3.55 euros for the H100 SXM, calculated at the European Central Bank (ECB) reference rate of 2 October 2026. Nebius has been charging the equivalent of 4.01 euros since 1 October 2026, and CoreWeave charges the equivalent of 43.87 euros for a node with eight H100s, which works out at 5.48 euros per GPU. In the US East region, AWS charges the equivalent of 6.13 euros per GPU hour for the p5.48xlarge instance with eight H100s, according to the price tracker Vantage as of 3 October 2026. For the Azure VM ND96isr H100 v5, AzureSpeed lists the equivalent of 10.95 euros per GPU hour as of 26 September 2026 for Linux with usage-based billing in East US.

Scaleway has been charging 25.332 euros per hour for a node with eight H100 SXM since 1 June 2026, which works out at 3.17 euros per GPU. OVHcloud lists the H100 as a PCIe card at 2.80 euros net, while Lambda and Scaleway quote the SXM form factor.

...

On 1 October 2026, Nebius raised the H100 hour from the equivalent of 3.43 to 4.01 euros, and the B200 from 6.37 to 7.57 euros. On 17 September 2026, CoreWeave reported short-duration contracts of three to six months at roughly 36 million euros in revenue per megawatt per year.
